findings.message: The new guard against claiming that time gets logged misses the pre-fix wording and lets through sentences that make the claim. `TIME` only matches the words `time` or `hours`. Its `[^.]*` stops at the decimal point in amounts like "2.5", so "logs 2.5 h" and "logs 2.5 hours" never match. The old caption "Wednesday goes from 5.0 to 7.5 hours" has no 'log' word at all, so it doesn't match either. `accepted()` passes any sentence that contains 'draft' or 'suggest' anywhere, even when that word isn't about the time. So the test covers only the hero wording the reviewer named, not the whole class. Fix: make the claim check about the hours themselves, for example `(log|add|book|record|fill)\w*` near a number followed by `h` or `hours`, or `timesheet`, and use a sentence split that doesn't break on decimals. Require the accept or draft word to be in the same clause as the hours. Add the old mock caption and the old VTT cue as rejected cases.
findings.scenario: Change the mock caption back to its pre-fix text "amax logs 2.5 h to Contoso Portal (fictional) and asks the PM to approve the week." → the time-claim test still passes. Write "Commits log time and suggest fixes." in HERO_LEDE → it passes too, because accepted() matches 'suggest'.

findings.message: Other copies of the 'commits log time' claim are still there. PRODUCT.md ("commits close tasks and log time") is the source that AC-3 says every claim must match. README.md:3 and docs/roadmap.md:5 say "commits log time", and the public GitHub Pages landing at apps/mock/app/page.tsx:28 says "Commits log time". All of these now contradict the corrected marketing copy and modules/delivery/README.md:17. Fix: correct them in their own small change. At minimum, list PRODUCT.md so a later AC-3 check doesn't bring the old claim back.
findings.scenario: A reviewer checks the hero against PRODUCT.md, as AC-3 requires → PRODUCT.md says commits log time, so the old wording looks correct and could be restored.

findings.message: The fixed story skips a step the product enforces. Kasun's accepted hours 'land as a draft', and in the next cue the PM approves the week. But `modules/time/server/decide.ts:20` refuses to approve a week that isn't `submitted`, and nothing in the story submits it. The ProductVideo figcaption and the mock storyboard have the same gap. Fix: add 'Kasun submits the week' between accepting and approving, or describe approving as approving a submitted week.
findings.scenario: A viewer follows the captions: accept the draft, then the PM approves. In the product, approving that week throws "<week> is open, not submitted" until Kasun submits it.

findings.message: [design] The fix only covers the wording the last round quoted ('log(s) time'). It misses another sentence that makes the same false claim. The Problem card says 'Jira, Monday and Kantata expect someone to fill in the timesheet, move the card and update the forecast. In amax, agents do that bookkeeping over MCP'. That tells readers agents fill in the timesheet over MCP with nobody acting. In the product, `commitTimeHandler` only creates a `time.commit-draft` suggestion, and the entry is logged only when the person accepts it. The same text appears in the 062 mock section (`.specclaw/mock/index.html:2226` and `apps/mock/public/mock/index.html:2226`). The new guard can't catch it. `TIME` in `marketing-confirm.test.ts` only matches 'log/logs/logged … time/hours', so 'fill in the timesheet … agents do that bookkeeping' passes. Fix: reword the sentence in Problem.tsx and in the mock so time is drafted and the person accepts it. For example: 'In amax, agents draft the timesheet, move the card and update the forecast over MCP, and people accept the hours'. Then widen `TIME` to cover timesheet, fill in, record, track and bookkeeping, and add 'In amax, agents fill in the timesheet over MCP.' to the rejects table.
findings.scenario: Render /welcome → the Problem section says agents fill in the timesheet over MCP → the 'commit hours are drafted and accepted' test still passes because `TIME` doesn't match 'fill in the timesheet', so the auto-logging claim ships
